overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the OML by announcing at the start of its main open session, not at the meeting's beginning, that the meeting was being recorded; the other two allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 22 agenda failed to state 'open session' to account for the short open session held before the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that it was clear that the Committee would hold a short open session prior to convening in executive session and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair failed to declare that discussing collective bargaining strategy in open session would have a detrimental effect on the Committee's bargaining position.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the Chair made the required statement regarding detrimental effect prior to convening in executive session and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair failed to inform attendees at the start of the meeting that it was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Chair technically did not inform attendees “[a]t the beginning of the meeting” that the meeting was being recorded, we are constrained to find that the Committee violated the law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
